requirements.statement: Discover LAN peers with bounded expiry and interface-change recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Peer candidates appear and expire through the bounded native discovery lifecycle.
Interface changes recover without treating discovery data as authenticated identity.
The cross-platform vertical-slice acceptance task proves the packaged behavior.

requirements.statement: Authenticate peer pairing with fail-closed identity storage, transcript, certificate, and session controls.
acceptance_criteria: First pairing requires explicit local confirmation and binds the accepted protocol transcript.
Reconnect, revocation, timeout, replay, role, and certificate failures close without fallback.
macOS, Windows, and qualified Linux storage participate in cross-platform acceptance.

requirements.statement: Offer one file, require explicit receiver acceptance, transfer it over an authenticated encrypted session, and commit it atomically.
acceptance_criteria: Two real processes transfer identical bytes only after explicit receiver acceptance.
Hostile metadata and failed integrity checks cannot escape or commit through storage.
Cross-platform acceptance proves authenticated identity and atomic destination commit.

requirements.statement: Expose peer selection, pairing, send, receive decision, and transfer progress through the Flutter application boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Presentation consumes application abstractions and never calls dart:ffi directly.
The packaged UI drives real native discovery, pairing, offer decisions, and progress.
Cross-platform acceptance verifies the complete user flow without claiming later production behavior.

requirements.statement: Cancel transfers with deterministic operation, callback, temporary-file, and session cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Local cancellation, remote withdrawal, process exit, and shutdown are idempotent.
Failed or cancelled transfers leave no committed partial file or stale temporary artifact.
The vertical-slice acceptance task proves cancellation through the packaged application.

requirements.statement: Transfer bounded multi-file manifests and directory trees.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest and path validation bound collections and preserve destination containment.
Production adapters and Flutter flow expose multi-file and directory transfers.
Final P1 acceptance proves complete and rejected manifest behavior.

requirements.statement: Schedule chunks with bounded backpressure, fairness, cancellation, and observable rate reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Chunk and queue limits prevent unbounded memory or sender dominance.
Rate and progress reporting remain monotonic across production adapters.
Final P1 acceptance exercises constrained and concurrent transfer schedules.

requirements.statement: Resume authenticated transfers after reconnect or process restart from bounded durable state.
acceptance_criteria: Resume state is versioned, bounded, and tied to the authenticated peer and manifest.
Corrupt, stale, or mismatched state fails closed without committing partial data.
Final P1 acceptance proves reconnect and process-restart recovery.

requirements.statement: Select contained destinations and apply an explicit collision policy before commit.
acceptance_criteria: Destination selection remains inside the approved root across supported platforms.
Existing-file collisions require an explicit deterministic policy.
Final P1 acceptance covers collision, traversal, and link-boundary rejection.

requirements.statement: Prove large-file, low-space, sleep-wake, and network-change behavior across supported platforms.
acceptance_criteria: macOS, Windows, and Linux evidence covers large files and low-space failure.
Sleep-wake and network changes recover or fail with deterministic cleanup.
The final P1 acceptance task records the cross-platform evidence before closing the milestone.
